model:
The maps illustrate the changes that have taken place in the village of Ashford between 1995 and the present day.
Overall, Ashford has become considerably more developed, with a large area of farmland being replaced by housing and new facilities being added for residents and drivers. The basic layout of the village, however, with the main road running from west to east, has remained the same.
The most significant change has occurred to the north of the main road, where the farmland that existed in 1995 has been converted into a housing estate. The main road has also been extended eastwards by means of a new bridge across the river, which now connects the village to the land on the other side.
South of the main road, the school in the south-west has been considerably enlarged, and the row of shops has been replaced by a supermarket. A car park has been built directly behind the supermarket, presumably to serve its customers. The houses in the south-east of the village are the only feature that appears to have remained unchanged.
modelNotes: Present perfect edilgen: has been converted, has been replaced, has been built.
Konum dili: to the north of, in the south-west, eastwards, across the river.
